title: Oscar and the Cellar
premise: Folklorist Xanthe Blackwood arrives in the isolated village of Hollowmere to record its songs, only to discover every ballad ends at the same missing verse. When an excavation crew unearths a cellar door sealed from the inside, Xanthe is pulled through into a liminal dark where the village's founders bargained away their children's voices to buy survival from something older than hunger. Guided by the ghost-choir of those sacrificed children and the unlikely found family of a gravedigger's daughter and a defrocked priest, Xanthe learns he was summoned because his blood completes the founders' line — the ritual demands a new voice to replace the ones spent centuries ago. In the end, Xanthe refuses to pay the price alone: he teaches the choir his own song, breaking the bargain by giving the dead back their names, though it costs him his hearing and leaves him forever unable to sing what he saved.
about_author: Wren Ishikawa is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing funeral hymns in coastal villages before turning to horror. They write in the margins of old songbooks and claim they have never once finished singing a folk song all the way through.

chapters.title: The Verse Nobody Sings
chapters.summary: Xanthe Blackwood arrives in Hollowmere, recording villagers who each stop at the same broken verse of a lullaby. POV: Xanthe. The emotional beat is uneasy curiosity curdling into dread as he realizes the omission is universal, deliberate, and afraid.

chapters.title: What the Spade Found
chapters.summary: An excavation crew unearths a stone door beneath the chapel, sealed with iron from the inside. That night Xanthe dreams of a choir singing his name. POV: alternating Xanthe and crew foreman Bram. The beat is denial — the village closes ranks, and Xanthe chooses to stay.

chapters.title: Counted Doors, Counted Names
chapters.summary: Xanthe befriends Maren, the gravedigger's daughter who keeps her own tallies of the missing, and Father Ellery, defrocked for asking about the founders' ledger. POV: Maren. The beat is tentative trust — three lonely people recognizing each other's vigilance as kinship.

chapters.title: Pulled Through
chapters.summary: The door opens for Xanthe specifically; hands of root and rope drag him into the cellar-dark where time pools like standing water. POV: Xanthe. The beat is terror and disorientation as he meets the Thing Below, which speaks politely and calls him 'the last verse.'

chapters.title: The Founders' Bargain
chapters.summary: In the dark, the ghost-choir of sacrificed children shows Xanthe the truth: the founders bought the village's survival with their children's voices, renewed every century. POV: the choir collectively. The beat is grief — the horror is not the monster but the arithmetic that fed it.

chapters.title: Above, the Waiting
chapters.summary: Maren and Ellery dig toward the sealed door while the village, corrupted by proximity to the bargain, begins humming the lullaby in unison. POV: Maren. The beat is desperate loyalty — she will not let the village choose Xanthe the way it once chose her great-aunt.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: The Thing offers Xanthe a deal: sing the replacement verse and live richly while another pays later. He sees visions of comfort built on borrowed throats. POV: Xanthe. The beat is temptation — power offered gently, and how easily survival justifies cruelty.

chapters.title: Names Given Back
chapters.summary: Xanthe instead begins teaching the choir their own stolen names and verses, restoring each child's song one by one; the Thing weakens as its food remembers itself. POV: Ellery. The beat is defiant hope — faith rebuilt not in God but in refusing to let the dead stay voiceless.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Climax: the village breaks through just as the Thing makes its final demand. Xanthe sings the completed lullaby with the whole choir, Maren and Ellery holding the door against the founders' angry descendants. The bargain shatters. The beat is sacrificial triumph at terrible cost.

chapters.title: A Song He Cannot Hear
chapters.summary: Resolution: Xanthe emerges deaf but alive; Hollowmere's children sing freely for the first time in centuries. Maren writes down what he mouths; Ellery buries the ledger. POV: Maren. The beat is bittersweet peace — found family keeping watch over a silence that was finally chosen.
